# Influence diagram

[Previous: Whiteboard](./whiteboard.md) | [Workflow](../workflow.md) | [Next: Decision tree](./decision_tree.md)

Structure the decision model using decisions, uncertainties, utilities, and their relationships. Inspect model inputs before interpreting calculated results. See [Influence diagrams](../../domain/influence_diagram.md) for arrow meanings, information timing, and input checks.

## Overview and navigation

### Open the influence diagram

Select **Influence Diagram** in the sidebar to view and work on the decision model.

![Influence Diagram sidebar entry](<../figures/influence_diagram/button - Influence Diagram.png>)

### Structure the influence diagram

Use the influence diagram to represent decisions, uncertainties, utilities, and their relationships. Arrows into a value node specify value dependencies; arrows into a decision specify information available before choosing; arrows into an uncertainty require the corresponding conditional probabilities. Do not add an information arrow merely to make a connection: it changes what the decision is allowed to know.

![Influence diagram page](<../figures/influence_diagram/page - Influence diagram.png>)

> [!WARNING]
> An arrow on an influence diagram only means a possible relationship. The absence of an arrow means no possible direct relationship. Therefore, an absence of arrow is a stronger message than the presence of one.

## Choose how to work with the diagram

### Use the diagram toolbar

The toolbar provides view modes, canvas navigation, layout controls, issue actions, and expected-value metrics.

![Influence diagram toolbar](<../figures/influence_diagram/menu - Influence diagram toolbar.png>)

### Choose a diagram view

Switch between **Card view** for issue details and **Shape view** for classic influence diagram symbols.

![Diagram view selector](<../figures/influence_diagram/field - Diagram view.png>)

### Choose a diagram interaction mode

Switch between pan and selection modes depending on whether you want to move around the canvas or select nodes.

![Influence diagram tool mode selector](<../figures/influence_diagram/field - Tool modes.png>)

## Add an issue

### Create an issue from the diagram

Select **Create Issue** in the diagram toolbar to open the issue creation form.

![Create Issue button in the influence diagram](<../figures/influence_diagram/button - Create Issue.png>)

### Describe a diagram issue

Enter the new issue's details and classification in the creation popup.

![Create Issue popup in the influence diagram](<../figures/influence_diagram/popup - Create Issue.png>)

## Connect issues and manage restrictions

### Add an arc

In **Shape view**, hover over the source issue and select the **+** control on its right. Choose a target from **Add arc to**; the arrow points from source to target. Alternatively, drag from the source control to the target node.
In **Diagram view**, click and drag from the tail node to the head node.

Add only a relationship supported by the model: an arrow into a decision represents information available before that decision. Check the target's probability or utility inputs after changing its parents.

![Add arc target menu](<../figures/influence_diagram/menu - Add arc.png>)

### Open an arc's actions

Hover over an arc to reveal its action control. For an arc into a decision or uncertainty, select the three dots to open its restriction table. For an arc into a Utility issue, select the trash icon to open the deletion confirmation instead.

![Arc action control](<../figures/influence_diagram/button - Arc actions.png>)

### Add, change, or remove restrictions

In the restriction table, rows are source states and columns are target states. A switch on means the combination is allowed; switch it off to restrict that target state for the source state. To change a restriction, adjust the relevant switches; to remove one, switch the combination back on. Changes save as you toggle. A restricted arc is dashed. Restrictions exclude combinations; they are not probability estimates. Review the probability table after changes, and use any warning tooltip to understand why a switch is unavailable or a restriction is invalid.

![Arc restriction table](<../figures/influence_diagram/window - Restriction Table.png>)

### Delete an arc

For an arc into a decision or uncertainty, open its restriction table and select the trash icon. For an arc into a Utility issue, select the trash icon shown when hovering over the arc. Check the source and target in the **Delete Edge** confirmation, then select **Delete**, or **Cancel** to keep it. Deleting the arc removes the relationship and its restrictions; review affected probability or utility inputs and results afterward.

![Delete edge confirmation](<../figures/influence_diagram/window - Delete Arc.png>)

## Inspect nodes and model inputs

### Inspect an issue node

An issue node displays the issue within the model and provides access to its actions.

![Uncertainty issue node](<../figures/influence_diagram/card - Issue node.png>)

### Open issue-specific actions

Use a node's action menu to access editing and model inputs such as the uncertainty's probability table.

![Issue actions menu](<../figures/influence_diagram/menu - Issue actions.png>)

### Review uncertainty probabilities

Enter probabilities as fractions from 0 to 1, not percentages: use 0.4 rather than 40 for 40%. Leave each edited cell to save it, then check that every applicable parent-state row sums to 1. Complete all required rows; a cell disabled by a restriction is not a missing input to overwrite. Record the evidence behind the estimates in the issue description or decision record.

![Weather probability table](<../figures/influence_diagram/window - Probability Table.png>)

### Enter values in a utility table

When a value depends only on one decision or uncertainty, enter its contribution in the **Utility** field for each option or outcome in the issue editor; a separate Utility issue is not accepted by Prisma. See the Issues guide for editing issue details.

When a value depends jointly on two or more issues, create a **Utility** issue and connect each parent to it. In Card view, open the Utility issue's **Issue actions** menu and select **Utility Table**. Each row represents a combination of parent states; enter its value under **Default metric** and leave the cell to save. State utilities and Utility tables both contribute additively to the model's total value, so do not count the same effect twice.

![Success utility table with two parent uncertainties](<../figures/influence_diagram/window - Utility Table.png>)

Select **Layout controls** to view the available options for arranging the diagram.

## Explore states and alternative views

### Expand diagram cards

Select **Expand All** to reveal the states of the diagram's decision and uncertainty cards. Expanding, collapsing, zooming, or fitting the view changes the presentation, not the model's dependencies or probability inputs.

![Expand All button in the influence diagram](<../figures/influence_diagram/button - Expand All.png>)

### Inspect expanded issue states

Expanded cards expose decision options and uncertainty outcomes directly in the diagram; use **Collapse All** to return to compact cards.

![Influence diagram with expanded cards](<../figures/influence_diagram/page - Influence diagram expanded.png>)

### Read the shape view

Shape view presents the same model with classic influence diagram symbols instead of detailed issue cards.

![Influence diagram in shape view](<../figures/influence_diagram/page - Influence diagram shape view.png>)

## Review calculated results

### Review model value metrics

Read the toolbar's expected-value metrics to inspect the model's calculated results. An expected value is not a guaranteed outcome. Check whether node outcomes are selected for conditional exploration, and clear unintended selections before interpreting an unconditional baseline. After editing inputs, wait for recalculation and review warnings before relying on the displayed values.

![Expected-value metrics in the influence diagram](<../figures/influence_diagram/card - Expected value metrics.png>)

### Read a decision's policy table

In Card view, open a decision's **Issue actions** menu and select **Policy Table**. In Shape view, hover over the decision and use its policy-table control. The table is a solver result, not an input: when information parents are shown, each row lists a combination of their states; each column is an option for that decision. A **1** marks the option selected by the optimal policy for that row; **0** means it is not selected. If no parent states are shown, the table has a single policy row.

Use the table to see how the recommended choice depends on information available before the decision. It reflects the model's structure, restrictions, probabilities and values, so revisit those assumptions before acting. The policy table is calculated for the base model rather than the selected what-if scenario.

![Event selection policy table](<../figures/influence_diagram/window - Policy Table.png>)

## Explore what-if scenarios

In Card view, expand a decision or uncertainty and select an option or outcome. Selecting an option forces that decision; selecting an outcome treats it as hard evidence. Selections can be combined across issues. Select the same state again to deselect it, or select another state on that issue to replace it. In Shape view, hover over a decision or uncertainty and use its states control to make the same selections.

The toolbar shows **Base EV** for the unconditioned model and **Scenario EV** for the selected states; the delta is Scenario EV minus Base EV. Wait for recalculation and check for warnings. A scenario is a conditional exploration, not a change to the model's probability inputs or a guaranteed outcome. Clear all selections to return to the baseline.

![Selected decision and scenario expected value in the influence diagram](<../figures/influence_diagram/page - What-if scenario.png>)
